top_story.headline: A presidential committee filed 28 Form 99s in two days that are hourly election vote-count logs, not campaign finance reports
top_story.dek: The 'fraud' and 'whistleblower' keyword hits come from the filer's own department name and from disclaimers that vote-total decreases are not called fraud.
paragraphs: Cory Steele for President (C00949545) is listed in FEC records as a Republican presidential committee for Cory James Steele, with a mailing address in Waterloo, Iowa. It had 28 miscellaneous Form 99 submissions received Nov. 5 and 6, four on Nov. 5 and 24 on Nov. 6. Twenty-five are numbered 'Hourly Examination Update' logs that recite vote tallies for races including the Mississippi, Alaska and Texas Senate contests and the Kansas, New York and Wisconsin governor races. The other three are a 'Founding Logic Annex', a 'Founder Doctrine Filing' and an 'Exposure Map' on mail-voting law. They are issued under the name Mind Of Monkey Studio. None of the 28 reports receipts, disbursements or any other campaign finance activity.

On the keyword hits, the text shows that 'whistleblower' and much of the 'fraud' language come from the filer's self-description, 'Cyberforce Whistleblower Election Fraud Monitoring Department'. The rest appears in repeated statements that a vote-total decrease 'is NOT called a vote switch or fraud', and in fact-checks of other people's claims. Those include a Lancaster, Pennsylvania video the filing says was recycled from 2024, and a Houston claim the filing says the FBI called false, citing Reuters. The filings do flag decreases as bad data at one of two measures. At 9:13 AM Central time on Nov. 6, South Carolina totals fell by 131 to 211 votes for each of four candidates. At 4:13 PM, one Wisconsin governor candidate's total fell by a single vote. The filer says only official canvasses can settle both.

Everything in these filings is the filer's own account, and DC Record has not verified the vote figures. One standalone filing also floats a thesis that media coverage decisions control when public scrutiny of vote counts ends. The same filing says the committee's findings 'establish no coordination'.

sections.headline: A Wisconsin House member answers an FEC letter on a removed $5,000 PAC contribution, and an Ohio senator's committee is closed out
paragraphs: Two filings are tagged to sitting lawmakers. Neither is late as far as the input shows. The termination filing was not read.

items: Rep. Scott Fitzgerald (R-WI) tells the FEC that a $5,000 Charter Communications Inc. PAC contribution dated 12/15/2024 was reported in error and has been removed. His committee, Scott Fitzgerald for Congress, was responding to an FEC RFAI on its amended July Quarterly Report (04/01/2025 to 06/30/2025), which the filing says was received 09/27/2026. It says the July report itself is correct and the Column B discrepancies came from earlier reports. It also says a $500 contribution's receipt date was corrected to 11/26/2024 and the April 15 Quarterly Report was amended to match the corrected Year-End 2024 Report. (Form 99)
Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH): Husted for OH Senate Republican Nominee Fund 2026 has a Termination Approval filing. The FEC received it 11/06. (Filing)

sections.headline: A candidate forgives $650,000 in personal loans, a PAC and a candidate committee file closeout and address notices, and one committee files 28 election-count logs
paragraphs: Thirty-three non-lawmaker Form 99s came in, 28 of them from Cory Steele for President. The Steele filings are listed after the other five, in the order of the hourly measure they report. Times in the Steele items are Central time (CT), as the filer labels them. Red-flag keywords hit only the Steele filings, and the Top Story explains what they do and do not show.

items: Razack for Congress tells the FEC that the remaining $650,000 in loans of personal funds by candidate Nizam Razack are forgiven. FEC records list Nizam Razack as a Republican candidate in an open Florida House seat. The filing is a one-line statement titled 'Loan Forgiveness' and gives no further detail. (Form 99)

Alliance for American Innovation and Rights files a free-text statement of termination saying it has ceased all activity and resolved its debts, obligations and residual funds. Treasurer Tamika La'Shon Hill signed it Nov. 6 for the Chicago-based hybrid PAC. It asks the FEC to approve the termination and mark the committee inactive. (Form 99)

Eversource Energy Political Action Committee submits a Form 1 statement of organization listing Duncan MacKay as treasurer and custodian of records. The form names Eversource Energy of Berlin, Connecticut as the connected organization, Ronald Smith as assistant treasurer and Bank of America in Hartford as its depository. The form is dated 11/06 while the FEC lists receipt as 11/05, and the new-versus-amended box is not legible. (Form 99)

PEOPLE PAC (PACCAR Inc Employees Organized for Political Leadership and Education PAC) submits a Form 1 statement of organization dated 11/05 that lists Karen Logan as treasurer. The Bellevue, Washington committee was sent an RFAI on 11/06 addressed to a different treasurer, Irene Song. The scan is poor and the new-versus-amended box is not clearly legible. (Form 99, RFAI)

SeanDavidRacing, a presidential committee, tells the FEC that all its mail should now go to 'Castle of America', 802 12th Avenue, Greeley, Colorado 80631. The filing is signed by Sean David Waltz as owner, and the header address is in Trachsville, Pennsylvania. Received 11/05. (Form 99)

blocks.text: Cory Steele for President: 25 hourly update filings, then three standalone filings

items: Cory Steele for President reports no decrease in any candidate total at its 6:13 PM CT Nov. 5 check. It gives the Mississippi Senate margin as 1,813 and says Westchester County, New York had scanned 26,929 emergency ballots. Received 11/05. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports no candidate-total decrease at its 7:13 PM CT Nov. 5 check and notes the AP called New York's 17th District for Conley. It says a House precinct-count field fell by 381 while party vote totals rose, and treats that as a field revision, not a decrease. Received 11/05. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President's 8:13 PM CT Nov. 5 filing includes a fact-check calling a Lancaster, Pennsylvania 'voter-registration fraud bust' video recycled from 2024. It also cites Reuters reporting an FBI statement that a Houston fraudulent-ballots claim is false. It reports no decrease in any race. Received 11/05. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports every watched total flat at its 9:13 PM CT Nov. 5 check. It also says a search for deceased-voter ballots found no official finding. Received 11/05. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports a Maricopa County batch at 10:13 PM CT Nov. 5 in which both candidates' totals rose. The filing says precincts went from 841 to 892 of 956. It reports no decreases. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports both New York governor candidates' totals rose at its 11:13 PM CT Nov. 5 check. The gains were 33,412 and 22,102. It carries a standing New York decrease of 53,486 until the December canvass. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President says nothing moved at its 12:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check. It lists a dozen races as flat and says South Carolina county certifications were due that day. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President's 1:13 AM CT Nov. 6 update, its 46th pass, reports all totals flat. It notes campaign counsel in Mississippi's Senate race exchanged preservation letters over affidavit ballots. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a third straight flat interval at its 2:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check, its 47th pass. It calls this the first scan under a Nov. 6 'application addendum'. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a fourth straight flat interval at its 3:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check. It says no certified South Carolina county figure had landed yet. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a fifth straight flat interval at its 4:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check. It says its first 'dove flight', its term for retrieving certified paper, returned empty. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports a sixth straight flat interval at 5:13 AM CT Nov. 6. It carries a Mississippi Republican Party claim that the affidavit pool is 'very abnormal' as unverified. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a seventh straight flat interval at its 6:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check, its 51st pass. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports an eighth straight flat interval at its 7:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check, its 52nd pass. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a ninth straight flat interval at its 8:13 AM CT Nov. 6 check, its 53rd pass. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports paired decreases of 119 to 211 votes for all four South Carolina Senate and governor candidates at 9:13 AM CT Nov. 6. It labels this bad data at one of two measures, 'NOT called a vote switch or fraud', and says certified county paper settles it. This is the first decrease after nine flat intervals. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports no new decrease at 10:13 AM CT Nov. 6 and says the South Carolina flag stands as logged. Wayne County, Michigan precincts rose from 744 to 762 of 770. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports South Carolina totals partly recovering at 11:13 AM CT Nov. 6. The Senate and governor gains were 105 to 191 votes per candidate. It says this does not withdraw the 9:13 AM flag. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President's 57th-pass update at 12:13 PM CT Nov. 6 reports no new decrease and covers a dozen races across three pages. It notes a Florida Escambia County commission race flipped from a 3-vote lead to a 19-vote lead for the other candidate after provisional review. A machine recount was set for Nov. 7. It also carries a Mississippi claim of about 14,000 affidavit ballots as unverified. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports five watched races rose at 1:13 PM CT Nov. 6 with no decrease. It gives the Kansas governor margin as 7,043. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports no new decrease at 2:13 PM CT Nov. 6. It gives the Mississippi Senate margin as 2,009 and says South Carolina totals are drifting upward. (Form 99)
Cory Steele for President reports a Mississippi Senate batch of +743 and +259 votes at 3:13 PM CT Nov. 6. The batch raised the margin to 2,493, and the filing says no decrease occurred. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports a one-vote paired decrease in the Wisconsin governor's race at 4:13 PM CT Nov. 6. One candidate's total fell from 1,440,990 to 1,440,989 while the other's rose by one. The filing says it is not called a vote switch or fraud and that Wisconsin's canvass will settle it. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports 2,017 uncounted absentee ballots found in Johnson County, Iowa at its 5:13 PM CT Nov. 6 update. The filing says the ballots were found Nov. 5 and left out of the unofficial results. It says the Iowa Secretary of State ordered an audit due Nov. 9. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President reports Mississippi affidavit-ballot figures and a Georgia memory-card failure at its 6:13 PM CT Nov. 6 update. The Mississippi Secretary of State's office reportedly said counties had reviewed 11,202 affidavit ballots, accepting 8,717 and rejecting 2,485. In Seminole County, Georgia, the filing says a corrected upload flipped a House District 154 lead by 262 votes, with an open Secretary of State investigation. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President files a 'Founding Logic Annex' mapping the Federalist Papers and other founding documents onto its audit rules. The two-page annex says it 'is not evidence about any count'. It also invokes Executive Order 13848, with an assessment due Dec. 18. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President files a 'Founder Doctrine Filing' proposing mandatory nationwide 24-hour elections. It also argues that whoever controls when scrutiny ends controls what scrutiny never sees, and attributes that to media coverage decisions as the founder's thesis. It adds that its findings 'establish no coordination'. (Form 99)

Cory Steele for President files an 'Exposure Map' of emergency election law and the possibility of ballot stuffing from 2020 to 2026. The filing says it measures possibility, not occurrence. It cites its own audits finding ballots counted above registration in only 11 of 12,921 jurisdiction-elections, all paperwork errors. (Form 99)

sections.headline: $150,000 in new independent expenditures
paragraphs: 1 new independent expenditures of $50K or more, $150,000 in all. Largest target: Julia Letlow (support, $150,000).

items: Accountability Project Inc: $150,000

blocks.text: Independent expenditures of $50K+ reported since 11/4/2026 (24/48-hour notices plus regular reports), counting only items not shown in an earlier edition. A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.

footer.coverage_window: FEC RFAI (FRQ) and Form 99 filings received Nov. 4 to Nov. 7, 2026. After deduplication against prior editions, 90 new filings: 53 RFAIs, 34 Form 99s and 3 terminations.
footer.sources: FEC filings API; FEC Schedule A/B itemized transactions.

The Money Out lookup for Trump National properties also timed out with HTTP 504. The RFAI texts in the input show headers only, with no numbered items or response due dates, so what each committee was asked cannot be stated. Termination filings were not read.

apod.title: De Gerlache-Kocher Massif
apod.caption: De Gerlache-Kocher massif looms on the visible horizon in this close-up of the edge of the Moon. The mountainous formation rises about 4 kilometers above its surroundings and is located very close to the lunar south pole.
